title: Practice proportionate self-regard in ordinary exchanges

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Proportionate self-regard recognizes real contribution, help and limits. Accepting a sound correction is different from agreeing with every criticism; humility does not require pretending to have contributed nothing.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Label draft: “Return here later.” Authorized rule: borrowed paper maps go in the blue folder on shelf A before the room closes 18:00; damaged maps go to the staffed desk. Jo wrote the draft, Rae supplied the rule and Kim notices that “here” has no fixed referent. No other contribution or intention is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Judge Kim’s correction against the rule, revise the label and credit contributions accurately. Keep your own actual work in the account.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A critic recommends removing a necessary return deadline to make the label prettier. Does humility require agreement?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A corrected label specifies blue folder/shelf A/before 18:00 and the damage exception. Kim’s location criticism is sound but does not itself cover timing or damage. Later fiction: one reader follows the correct destination but no real return occurs. Partial: accept praise/criticism without checking the rule. Incorrect: claim sole authorship or deny writing the original text.
criteria: Contributions and limits are accurately named
Correction is checked against the standard
Humility does not mean automatic agreement

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Explain the deadline’s actual function and seek a clearer design that preserves it. Respectful evidence-based disagreement can be proportionate self-regard.
